summary: Implemented PrimaryNavigationService.cs as a sealed class backed by a destination list and a nullable active destination.
Register(destinations) stores the list and resets _activeDestination to null.
NavigateTo(id) finds the destination by Id; if not found or already active, returns without change or event; otherwise sets ActiveDestination and fires ActiveDestinationChanged once.
FindDestination uses a foreach loop for linear lookup (list is always small).

comments.note: PrimaryNavigationService.cs: FindDestination uses a foreach loop over _destinations for linear ID lookup. For small destination lists (typically 3–5 rail items) this is perfectly appropriate. If destinations grow large, a Dictionary<string, PrimaryDestination> keyed by Id would be faster, but that would be premature optimisation here.

PrimaryNavigationService.cs: Register() resets _activeDestination to null unconditionally. If an active destination's Id still exists in the new list, the caller must re-call NavigateTo to re-select it. This is intentional defensive behaviour (caller must be explicit), but is worth noting in QA tests.

comments.note: PrimaryNavigationService.cs: Register(destinations) assigns the reference directly to _destinations without a null guard. With C# nullable reference types enabled, the non-nullable IReadOnlyList<PrimaryDestination> parameter gives a compile-time guarantee that null cannot be passed, so no runtime guard is needed. Confirmed acceptable.

[documentation-forward] IPrimaryNavigationService.cs: Interface has no XML doc comments. Register(destinations) semantics — that it unconditionally resets ActiveDestination to null even if the same destination ID exists in the new list — is non-obvious and should be documented. NavigateTo(destinationId) and the no-op invariants (unknown ID, already-active ID) also warrant brief summaries.

[documentation-forward] PrimaryDestination.cs: The sealed record PrimaryDestination(string Id, string Title, object RootViewModel) lacks XML doc comments. The RootViewModel property (typed as object by design) benefits from a note explaining why it is untyped (passed directly to Avalonia ViewLocator, which accepts object).
